key_insight: SDE-induced kernels have a sequentially semiseparable (SSS) covariance structure that enables linear-time kernel inference directly on the covariance matrix, not just on latent state estimates.
engineering_relevance: This makes Gaussian process regression and kernel-based regularization practical for large-scale system identification and machine-learning problems with Matérn, spline, and related kernels.
method: Represent the observed kernel covariance as an SSS matrix derived from an LTI SDE.
Use generator-level recursions for factorization, linear solves, log determinants, posterior covariance, and sampling.
Extend the same recursions to analytic marginal-likelihood gradients and kernel-based regularization with minor modifications.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that verify the accuracy of the recursions and demonstrate posterior inference and sampling on representative SDE-induced kernels.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to kernels with an SDE/SSS structure, so performance and applicability depend on whether the kernel admits an efficient SSS representation.
paper_title: On the Sequentially Semiseparable Structure of SDE-Induced Kernels and Efficient Algorithms for Kernel-Based Estimation Problems
